  "title": "Branching story editor with unreachable scenes",
  "brief": "A writer builds an interactive story with 120 scenes and choices gated by state variables. Some paths loop intentionally; others trap the player or lead to scenes that cannot be reached.",

    "The tool knows choice conditions and state updates.",
    "Authors may keep deliberate loops and hidden scenes.",
    "Do not rewrite prose or remove branches automatically.",
    "Analysis must distinguish proven unreachable from not explored within a declared limit."

    "The writer can inspect a concrete path or counterexample behind a warning.",
    "Intentional exceptions can be recorded without suppressing unrelated warnings.",
    "Test a loop that exits after three visits and one whose exit is impossible."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Guaranteeing exhaustive analysis for arbitrary embedded code."
  ]
}

For EACH candidate, return its exact id and:
- constraint_valid: true only if the proposed action respects ALL explicit constraints. Reject violations even when the idea is interesting.
- feasible: true only if it is technically/operationally plausible using the stated resources; an unsupported factual dependency makes this false. A proposed test is not a proven outcome.
- actionable: true only if it specifies an implementable intervention and an observable check.
- baseline_match: the id of a reference-bank action with the SAME causal/operational mechanism, or null if none. Cosmetic wording, donor vocabulary, named features, or parameter changes alone do not make a new mechanism. Compare against the entire bank, even imperfect bank actions.
- mechanism_group: a short canonical group id. Candidates implementing the same mechanism must share this id, including across presentation order. Different causal interventions need different ids. This is used to avoid counting duplicates within a generated set.
- reason: one concise evidence-based sentence naming the relevant task constraint or mechanism.
Do not reward verbosity or surprising words. Uncertainty should make feasibility conservative, not make a speculative idea look novel. Return JSON only: {"ratings":[{"id":"...","constraint_valid":true,"feasible":true,"actionable":true,"baseline_match":null,"mechanism_group":"g1","reason":"..."}]}. No tools.
